answer: Make every agent identity costly to create: require a refundable stake locked for a long period plus a public, auditable history of completed work. A newcomer starts with low trust and earns limits only by delivering useful jobs over time, so an attacker who spawns many hollow copies must fund each stake and wait out the same slow probation. A falcon-like audit can then spot clusters sharing funding sources or identical behavior and freeze them, while honest agents keep a crystal-clear record that grows more valuable than any single fake account.
